m: roga m. (√ ruj) ‘breaking up of strength’, disease, infirmity, sickness (also personified as an evil demon), AV. &c. &c.
a: rogaḥ [ruj-ghañ] A disease, sickness, malady, distemper, infirmity; saṃtāpayaṃti kamapathyabhujaṃ na rogāḥ H. 3. 117; bhoge rogabhayaṃ Bh. 3. 35. Comp. — aṃtakaḥ, -hṛt m. a physician. — āyatanaṃ the body. — ārta, -anvita, -grasta, — bhāj a. afflicted with disease, sick. — upaśamaḥ cure or alleviation of disease. — ghna a. curative, medicinal. — ghnaṃ 1 a medicine. 2 the science of medicine. — bhūḥ f. the body. — rājaḥ consumption. — lakṣaṇaṃ the symptoms of a disease. — śāṃtakaḥ a physician. — śāṃtiḥ f. alleviation or cure of a disease. — śilā red arsenic. — śreṣṭhaḥ fever. — haṃ a drug. — han m. a physician. — hara a. curative. — (raṃ) a medicine. — hārin a. curative. ( — m.) a physician.

m: roma—harṣa m. the bristling of the h˚ of the body, thrill (caused by joy, fear, cold &c.), MBh.; R. &c.
roma—harṣaṇa mfn. causing the h˚ to bristle or stand erect (through excessive joy or terror), MBh.; R. &c.
roma—harṣaṇa m. Terminalia Bellerica (the nuts of which are used as dice), L.
N. of Sūta (the pupil of Vyāsa and supposed narrator of the Purāṇas), Pur.
of the father of Sūta, BhP.
